reply_text:
I found one new 2023 candidate, and it is weak. Six pages opened and none of them had Hassabis making a dated AI forecast in his own words. I didn't open the pages behind any of the four claims already on file, so none of them turn up again here.

- **The one candidate: a private beta of the Sparrow chatbot "some time in 2023".** It comes from TIME's interview of 12 January 2023, which reported that DeepMind was "considering releasing" the chatbot then. I only read it on LessWrong, which reposts TIME's text, because TIME's own page cut off before that passage and so did a second copy on the MIT CBMM site. The sentence is the journalist's summary. Only the words "private beta" are marked as his. It is also a company product plan rather than a forecast about what AI can do. A Sparrow beta never seems to have shipped.
- **The Swiss newspaper interview (NZZ, 6 February 2023; English translation by ACM Ubiquity, October 2023):** nothing with a date. He says today's large models lack memory and planning and that a true general AI is not there yet. The only date is the editor's note that Bard would come out "in the coming weeks", which aren't Hassabis's words.
- **The Guardian, October 2023:** I only saw the Slashdot excerpt of it. He says "god-like" AI is "a long time away", which has no date. He also says current systems "aren't of risk but the next few generations may be" — that is about risk, not about when something arrives.
- **The June 2023 Wired interview on Gemini:** the copy I opened was only a teaser. A Medium post in the search results says Gemini "could be released as soon as this winter", but those are the blogger's words and I didn't see the original. All six page openings and 10 of the 12 searches are used.
